 THE TIMES OF INDIA | Oct 27, 2026, 15:00:36 IST SUMMARY India vs New Zealand Live Score, 3rd T20: India will have the chance to put their recent T20I troubles behind them and seal the series against New Zealand when the two sides meet in the third match at Hnry Stadium in Wellington on Tuesday. Shreyas Iyer’s team have won the opening two games and will be keen to carry that momentum into a contest where strong winds and potentially tricky weather could test their adaptability. 
 The Men in Blue have endured a mixed run since lifting the T20 World Cup. Defeats in Ireland, a disappointing 4-0 series loss in England and a 2-2 draw against the West Indies at home highlighted their inability to finish matches consistently. The recent victories in New Zealand, however, have provided encouraging signs of progress. 
 India began the tour with a successful chase of 225 before producing a resilient performance in the second T20I. After slipping to 70/5, they recovered to chase down New Zealand’s 180, with Naman Dhir, Tilak Varma and Nitish Kumar Reddy holding their nerve under pressure. 
 Teenager Vaibhav Sooryavanshi is expected to feature again at No.3, with Ishan Kishan unavailable for the third match. The youngster will be eager to make the most of the opportunity as India look to maintain their aggressive approach. 
 Bowling coach Morne Morkel has emphasised the need to raise standards and avoid excuses after the team’s earlier inconsistencies. Wellington’s swirling winds could make conditions challenging, although the forecast suggests the rain should clear before the scheduled 8 PM local start. 
 New Zealand will be without Matt Henry for the remainder of the series, while Lockie Ferguson is also set to miss the match. Despite those absences, the hosts will look to respond after losing the first two games. India have won 18 of their 21 T20Is against New Zealand this decade and will aim to add another victory to that impressive record while securing the series. Commentary 
 11:51 (IST) Oct 27 IND vs NZ Live Score: Bhuvneshwar Kumar faces tough comeback in T20Is Veteran pacer Bhuvneshwar Kumar has struggled to make an impact since returning to India’s T20I setup after a four-year absence, putting himself under pressure ahead of the third T20I against New Zealand. India will clash against New Zealand in the third of five-match T20I series on Tuesday in Wellington at the Hnry Stadium. 
 Recalled to the squad on the back of his impressive performances in the Indian Premier League (IPL), the right-arm seamer has proved expensive in the first two matches and will be eager to bounce back as India look to strengthen their position in the series.
 Kumar returned to India’s T20I setup after a four-year absence, earning a place in the squad for the series against New Zealand. However, the experienced pacer has struggled to contain the opposition’s batters in the first two matches, conceding runs at an expensive rate.
 In the opening T20I, New Zealand posted a massive 225/4, with Kumar going wicketless and leaking 49 runs in his four overs. The veteran seamer endured another expensive outing in the second T20I, conceding 50 runs and taking one wicket as New Zealand posted 180/5. With the third match approaching, Kumar will be eager to regain his rhythm and deliver a more economical spell, with his place in the playing XI potentially under scrutiny after back-to-back costly performances. 
 11:35 (IST) Oct 27 IND vs NZ Live Score: Arshdeep Singh two scalps away from becoming 1st Indian to take 150 T20I wickets India’s star pacer Arshdeep Singh is on the cusp of a significant milestone in T20 cricket, with history within touching distance. The left-arm seamer is just two wickets away from reaching the milestone of 150 T20I wickets, which would make him the first Indian bowler to achieve the feat. Singh will be in action on Tuesday as India take on New Zealand in the third T20I of the five-match series at Wellington’s Hnry Stadium. 
 Singh has claimed 148 wickets in 101 T20I matches at an impressive average of 20.41 and an economy rate of 8.65, including a five-wicket haul. He is currently India’s leading wicket-taker in the format and ranks 10th on the all-time list, leaving him just two wickets short of the 150-wicket milestone. 11:20 (IST) Oct 27 IND vs NZ Live Score: 'Vaibhav Sooryavanshi needs to wait'- Ex-India cricketer wants youngster dropped after just one innings
 India stands on the brink of clinching the T20I series against New Zealand as they eye a win in Wellington. Subramaniam Badrinath proposes a strategic change by swapping Vaibhav Sooryavanshi with Varun Chakaravarthy for the pivotal third match, noting Sooryavanshi's difficulties in an atypical role. Badrinath also emphasizes the importance of keeping Sanju Samson in the lineup, reflecting on India's solid performance against New Zealand over the past decade.  11:10 (IST) Oct 27 IND vs NZ Live Score: New Zealand admit frustration as hosts seek stronger finish against India New Zealand have shown promising spells in the opening two T20Is but have struggled to finish matches against India. Head coach Rob Walter acknowledged that his side had performed well for large portions of both games, only to fall short when it mattered most. The hosts will now look to address those shortcomings in Wellington, where they need a victory to keep the series alive.
 India’s ability to recover from difficult situations in the second match underlined the challenge facing New Zealand. With Matt Henry unavailable for the rest of the series and Lockie Ferguson missing the third game, the home side will need contributions across departments to stop India from completing a series win.
 11:00 (IST) Oct 27 IND vs NZ Live Score: India need to sharpen bowling and batting against spin Despite winning their first two matches in New Zealand, India still have areas to improve as they approach the third T20I. Bowling coach Morne Morkel has called for higher standards, particularly after the team's inconsistent performances in Ireland and England. Bowling execution and batting against spin remain important areas as India look to become more consistent across all phases of a match. 
 New Zealand’s spinners have taken eight wickets in the series at an economy rate of 8.25, making them a key threat for the visitors. India’s ability to manage that challenge, while maintaining their attacking intent, could prove decisive as they aim to seal the series in Wellington.
 10:50 (IST) Oct 27 IND vs NZ Live Score: India's middle-order response offers encouragement after second T20I scare India’s recovery in the second T20I was one of the biggest positives from their opening two matches in New Zealand. Chasing 181, the visitors found themselves in trouble at 70/5 before Naman Dhir, Tilak Varma and Nitish Kumar Reddy helped steer the innings towards a four-wicket win. 
 Their composure under pressure demonstrated the importance of partnerships and smart decision-making in a challenging chase. India had already shown their batting firepower by chasing 225 in the opening game, but the second match tested a different side of their game. The team will hope to build on that resilience when they face New Zealand in Wellington.

 10:40 (IST) Oct 27 IND vs NZ Live Score: India hold impressive T20I record against New Zealand this decade India have enjoyed a strong run against New Zealand in T20I cricket this decade. Including the T20 World Cup final in March, the Men in Blue have won 18 of their 21 matches against the Black Caps during this period. That record provides further confidence as Shreyas Iyer’s side prepare for the third T20I in Wellington. 
 New Zealand have often proved difficult opponents on major occasions, but the recent results have tilted the balance towards India in the shortest format. With the visitors leading the current series 2-0, another victory would strengthen their recent record and allow them to wrap up the contest before the final matches.
 10:30 (IST) Oct 27 IND vs NZ Live Score: New Zealand face bowling concerns with Matt Henry and Lockie Ferguson unavailable New Zealand will be without Matt Henry for the remainder of the T20I series, while Lockie Ferguson is also set to miss the third match in Wellington. The absences present a challenge for the hosts as they attempt to prevent India from securing the series. 
 However, New Zealand have depth in their fast-bowling resources and will hope their replacements can make an impact on a fresh surface. Their spinners have been more productive than the pace attack in the series so far, taking eight wickets at an economy rate of 8.25, compared with four wickets at 11.78 for the pacers. The hosts will need a stronger collective effort to stay alive in the contest.
 10:20 (IST) Oct 27 IND vs NZ Live Score: Shreyas Iyer's India one win away from sealing T20I series Shreyas Iyer’s India have moved within touching distance of a series victory after winning the first two T20Is against New Zealand. The captain will hope his side can finish the job in Wellington rather than leave the contest open heading into the remaining matches. India’s performances have improved since a difficult run in Ireland and England, although the drawn home series against the West Indies showed that consistency remains a work in progress.
 The opening two games in New Zealand have brought encouraging signs, with the batting unit producing a big chase before showing resilience under pressure. A third successive victory would give India a significant boost.
 10:10 (IST) Oct 27 IND vs NZ Live Score: Wellington wind could test India as weather adds another challenge Strong winds are expected to be a major talking point when India take on New Zealand in the third T20I in Wellington. Wind gusts of up to 55kph swept through the city on the eve of the match, while the forecast also included the possibility of rain on Tuesday. 
 Conditions are expected to improve before the scheduled 8 PM local start, although the wind could remain a factor. Morkel described the conditions as a new challenge for the Indian players and stressed the need to adapt rather than make excuses. India will hope their earlier experience of difficult conditions in Ireland helps them negotiate Wellington’s unpredictable weather.
 09:55 (IST) Oct 27 IND vs NZ Live Score: India need to keep aggressive approach after two encouraging wins India have made a promising start to the T20I series, showing the ability to attack from the outset and recover when placed under pressure. They chased down 225 in the opening match before overcoming a difficult position in the second game. After losing five wickets for 70 runs, India relied on Naman Dhir, Tilak Varma and Nitish Kumar Reddy to guide them towards victory. 
 The performances reflect the aggressive approach that the management wants the team to embrace. However, India will need to sustain that intent in Wellington, where conditions could make execution more difficult. Another win would seal the series and provide further evidence of progress.
 09:50 (IST) Oct 27 IND vs NZ Live Score: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi set for another opportunity as Ishan Kishan misses out Teenage opener Vaibhav Sooryavanshi is expected to retain his place in India’s line-up for the third T20I against New Zealand, with Ishan Kishan ruled out of the match. Sooryavanshi is likely to bat at No.3, giving the youngster another opportunity to establish himself in the side. 
 India have won both matches so far, and the team management is unlikely to make unnecessary changes to a combination that has delivered results. The contest in Wellington will provide Sooryavanshi with another chance to contribute as India look to maintain their aggressive approach and secure the series with a match to spare.
 09:45 (IST) Oct 27 IND vs NZ Live Score: Morne Morkel sends clear message to India players ahead of third T20I India bowling coach Morne Morkel has made it clear that the team must raise its standards as the New Zealand tour progresses. After allowing for the challenges of travel and jet lag during the opening matches, the management expects the players to improve their execution. Morkel acknowledged that India had been inconsistent in Ireland and England, but stressed that the team remains committed to an aggressive brand of cricket. 
 He wants the players to improve the small details that can make a difference in close contests. With India one win away from sealing the series, Wellington presents an opportunity to demonstrate that the progress is sustainable.
 09:40 (IST) Oct 27 IND vs NZ Live Score: From Ireland and England setbacks to New Zealand turnaround India’s recent T20I journey has been anything but straightforward. After winning the T20 World Cup, the team struggled to find consistency under new captain Shreyas Iyer. The difficulties began in Ireland, where India lost both matches while chasing, including a narrow one-run defeat. The England series proved even more disappointing, with the hosts winning 4-0. 
 India subsequently failed to secure a series victory against the West Indies at home, settling for a 2-2 draw. The opening two wins in New Zealand have offered a welcome change, but India will need to maintain their standards in Wellington if they are to complete the turnaround.

Shreyas Iyer’s team have won the opening two matches and need just one more victory to clinch the series. 
 The Men in Blue began their tour with a successful chase of 225 before recovering from 70/5 to beat New Zealand by four wickets in the second game. The results have provided a timely boost after a difficult run that included defeats in Ireland, a 4-0 series loss in England and a 2-2 draw against the West Indies at home.
 India vs New Zealand Live Score, 3rd T20: India will look to seal the T20I series against New Zealand when the teams meet in the third match at Hnry Stadium in Wellington on Tuesday. After a difficult run following their T20 World Cup triumph, Shreyas Iyer’s side have shown signs of recovery, winning the first two matches and moving within one victory of clinching the series.
India’s recent struggles began on the Ireland tour, where they lost both matches while chasing, before suffering a 4-0 defeat in England. The team also failed to secure a series win at home against the West Indies, with the visitors managing a 2-2 draw. Those setbacks exposed inconsistencies in both batting and bowling, prompting the management to demand higher standards.
The opening two matches in New Zealand have offered encouragement. India chased down 225 in the first T20I before recovering from 70/5 to secure a four-wicket victory in the second. Naman Dhir, Tilak Varma and Nitish Kumar Reddy played crucial roles in the comeback, while the bowlers restricted New Zealand to 180.
With Ishan Kishan ruled out of the third match, teenager Vaibhav Sooryavanshi is expected to get another opportunity at No.3. India will also need to adjust to Wellington’s challenging weather, with strong winds and the possibility of rain adding another layer of difficulty.
Bowling coach Morne Morkel has stressed the importance of maintaining an aggressive approach and eliminating excuses. New Zealand, meanwhile, will aim to stay competitive despite the absence of Matt Henry and Lockie Ferguson. India have won 18 of their 21 T20Is against New Zealand this decade, including the T20 World Cup final in March, and will hope to extend that record on Tuesday.
